Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the EverSecure Insurance Group Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. Instructions for queuing up will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to EverSecure Insurance Group's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Mark Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Laura Bennett, Chief Financial Officer; and Tom Ellis, Chief Underwriting Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to Mark Thompson.

Mark Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on EverSecure Insurance Group's performance for Q3 2024. We delivered strong results, driven by robust investment income yields, excellent combined ratio performance across all segments, favorable trends in customer acquisition costs, and positive impacts from updates to our actuarial assumptions.

Laura, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Laura Bennett: Thank you, Mark. Good morning, everyone. As Mark mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $1.2 billion, or $2.10 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included higher investment returns, disciplined underwriting, efficient customer growth, and reserve adjustments from refined actuarial views. Our combined ratio was 92.3%, reflecting effective underwriting and claims management. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with risk-based capital at 520% and book value per share at $95.50.

Let me expand on these highlights, starting with our investment income yield, which is a core driver of our earnings power. For context, we calculate this as annualized net investment income divided by the average amortized cost of our invested assets. This metric highlights the efficiency of our general account portfolio, which totals $185 billion as of quarter-end, supported by our substantial $120 billion float from property-casualty and life operations.

In Q3, we achieved a book yield of 4.25%, an increase of 45 basis points year-over-year and 15 basis points from Q2's 4.10%. This is our strongest quarterly yield since early 2008, benefiting from the sustained higher interest rate environment. Compared to our full-year 2023 yield of 3.85%, we're on track for the upper end of our 2024 guidance range of 4.10% to 4.30%. Stripping out a one-time $18 million gain from redeeming legacy high-yield municipal bonds, our core yield stood at a solid 4.18%, showing resilience independent of market swings.

Diving into portfolio components, fixed income forms the foundation at 72% of the portfolio, or $133 billion, accounting for 85% of our $1.95 billion in quarterly net investment income. Yields in this area rose to 4.45% from 3.95% last year, due to repositioning efforts we began in late 2022. We've increased exposure to investment-grade corporates to 28% from 24%, where BBB spreads over Treasuries narrowed to 115 basis points amid strong corporate health, yet delivering a 5.40% yield-to-worst. Our 18% allocation to mortgage-backed securities benefited from agency MBS offering 4.80% with low prepayment risks in the current rate environment. Treasuries and agencies make up 26%, providing liquidity at a 4.20% yield as the 10-year Treasury stayed near 4.15%.

Equities represent 10%, or $18.5 billion, yielding 3.20% from dividend income, with emphasis on stable dividend aristocrats such as Procter & Gamble and Johnson & Johnson, which offer protection during the S&P 500's 22% year-to-date gain. Our alternatives bucket, at 18% and including $12 billion in core-plus real estate and infrastructure through vehicles like Blackstone's BREIT and Brookfield partnerships, generated an impressive 5.80% yield. New commitments here show internal rates of return over 7%, countering REIT pressures like 5% cap rate tightening in multifamily properties.

Geographically, our U.S. holdings at 65% of assets led the yield gains, with domestic corporates and ABS at 4.65%, compared to 3.95% in Europe and Canada where we favor sovereigns like UK Gilts and Bunds following ECB rate reductions. In Asia-Pacific, our 12% slice in investment-grade emerging market bonds, such as Singapore SSA and Australian semis, yielded 4.75%, aided by ASEAN expansion and careful selection to sidestep China property issues. Diversification helped counter currency pressures, with hedging overlays adding just 8 basis points of cost.

From an asset-liability management perspective, our team performed exceptionally, extending duration to 5.8 years from 5.4 while securing reinvestment rates above 4.50% on $22 billion in maturities. The portfolio maintains an AA- rating, with 92% investment-grade assets—better than peers like MetLife at around 7% non-investment-grade. We've progressed on ESG goals, allocating $8 billion to sustainable bonds like green corporates from NextEra Energy at 4.60% yield, without losing return potential and aligning with regulations like the EU's SFDR and our net-zero by 2050 pledge.

This yield strength differentiates us strategically. Our P&C float expanded 6% year-over-year, unlike some competitors facing yield squeezes from reserve adjustments. We're gearing up for potential Fed rate cuts of 75 basis points by mid-2025 by building a $15 billion short-duration ladder at 4.80% and pursuing private credit opportunities through partners like Ares for 6-7% net yields matched to life liabilities. We use a conservative 4.50% total return assumption for reserving, creating a 60 basis point buffer over book yield.

For the outlook, we anticipate Q4 yields above 4.30%, with 2025 guidance of 4.40-4.60% assuming steady spreads and no downturn. This bolsters our 12% ROE goal and $1.2 billion share repurchase program. Potential risks like spread widening in office CMBS or yield curve inversion are mitigated by our 18-month liquidity cushion and interest rate swaps hedging 40% of duration risk.

Shifting to underwriting, our overall combined ratio for the quarter was 92.3%, improving 240 basis points from 94.7% a year ago and 50 basis points ahead of our guidance midpoint. This extends our streak of 11 consecutive quarters of progress, excluding catastrophes, thanks to sustained pricing and profitability efforts. Year-to-date, it's 93.1%, competitive with Progressive at 92.8% and Travelers at 94.2%.

The loss ratio came in at 66.5%, down 180 basis points year-over-year, supported by auto claim frequency returning to pre-COVID norms at 1.2 claims per policy year and $45 million in favorable prior-year development, or 1.2 points. Catastrophe losses were $220 million pretax, or 5.8 points, mainly from Hurricane Helene in the U.S. Southeast and European windstorm Erwin—matching our $200-250 million expectations. Excluding cats, the loss ratio was 60.7%.

The expense ratio improved 60 basis points to 25.8%, from efficiencies in our digital agency portal and 2% headcount reductions in support functions. We invested $15 million in AI for claims processing, cutting cycle times by 10 days.

By segment, personal lines, 55% of earned premiums at $4.2 billion, posted 90.2%, the best in five years and 310 basis points better year-over-year. Personal auto was 89.5%, with loss ratio at 62.1% after 8% rate gains, 35% telematics penetration—up from 22%—and stabilizing used car prices. Homeowners/other at 92.8% faced 7.2 points of cat impact from Helene but gained from 12% hikes in Florida and California, where we're non-renewing 15% of high-risk coastal policies amid reinsurance cost rises.

Commercial lines, 30% of premiums at $2.3 billion, achieved 94.1%, up 150 basis points. Middle-market P&C at 93.2%, with workers' comp loss ratio at 58% via our PPO network covering 85% of claims. Excess & surplus excelled at 91.5%, driven by 18% growth in habitational risks using climate-resilient models from RMS partnerships.

Specialty and international, 15% at $1.1 billion, delivered 89.7%. U.S. specialty at 88.4% from cyber portfolio tweaks, raising attachment points and ceding 20% more to Lloyd's. Europe/Asia at 92.1% reflected 4.1 cat points from Erwin and Thailand floods, countered by 10-15% rate adjustments in UK motor. Emerging markets like India added upside via 25% growth in low-frequency micro-insurance.

U.S. operations at 85% of premiums hit 91.8%, with Southeast at 95.2% from cats but Midwest/West below 90%. Europe was 93.5% due to 12% reinsurance rate hikes at January 1 renewal, while Asia-Pacific improved to 90.8% in non-cat lines like liability.

Ongoing pressures include 5% auto severity growth from labor and parts inflation, but offset by 15-point book value increase and 22% earned rates. Cat frequency is 1.25 times the 10-year average per Verisk, so we've raised all-peril cat loads to 8% in pricing. Year-to-date prior releases were $120 million at 85% confidence.

Our Underwrite 2.0 program with generative AI has reduced errors 18% and will expand to commercial next quarter. Apex Shield Re captive cuts secondary peril cessions 8%. We're exiting high-hazard homeowners in 10 states like Louisiana and shifting to data-driven fleet insurance, aiming for 92% ex-cat by year-end.

Guidance: full-year combined ratio 93.0-94.0%, Q4 ex-cat 91-92%, with 10-12% rate momentum for sub-93% long-term.

Next, customer acquisition cost trends, or CAC, remain central to our profitability. CAC captures all costs to onboard new policyholders—marketing, commissions, leads, onboarding, and overhead like analytics—tracked per policy and normalized for mix across auto, home, renters, and term life, benchmarked against Progressive, Allstate, and Lemonade.

Blended CAC was $238 per new policy in Q3, down 7% from $256 year-ago and 4% from Q2's $248—11 straight quarters of gains. Versus industry P&C average of $265 per NAIC data, our 10% edge supports a 4.2x LTV/CAC ratio, up from 3.8x.

By channel: Digital at 45% of acquisitions dropped 12% to $185, with Google DV360 and Meta optimizing CPC to $2.15 via AI creatives and propensity models boosting conversions 18% on high-intent terms. Telematics upsells cut app drop-offs 22%.

Agents/brokers at 30% fell 5% to $290, aided by portal APIs with Vertafore reducing quoting time 35%, tiered commissions, and retention bonuses clawing back 20%.

Partnerships at 25% plunged 22% to $142: Uber/Lyft auto via XCover at sub-$100; Amazon/Wayfair home at $160; ADP life adding 8,000 policies.

U.S. (72%) at $215, down 9% on softer non-standard auto competition and Prop 103 telematics savings. Europe (15%) at $312 flat from GDPR/Solvency II, but UK telco bundles help; PSD3 pilots target 15-20% cuts. Asia-Pacific (13%) at $168, down 14% via India JVs at $90 CAC and Gojek health.

Enablers: ML lead scoring on 50M policies hits 87% accuracy, saving $18M; multi-touch attribution shifts to CTV at 5.8x ROAS; GenAI chatbots deflect 65% agent queries.

We're targeting $210 by Q4 via embedded growth, exiting direct mail. Payback now 8 months, fueling 15% EPS growth. Focus on high-LTV bundles over transactional auto. First-party data from 25M app users counters privacy risks.

Finally, changes in actuarial assumptions drove $285 million pre-tax favorability, or 24% of $1.18 adjusted operating EPS, up 15% year-over-year. These stem from updated experience data, SOA studies, and analytics under VM-20 PBR, VM-31, and IFRS 17.

Mortality updates yielded $180 million favorable: Shifting to 2023 CSO with post-COVID tweaks, actual rates 4% below priors for ages 65+ in our $450 billion life/annuity block (2.5M policies), releasing reserves and dropping ratio to 102% NPV post-reinsurance ($140M net).

Lapse/surrender rates added $120 million: Down 1.2% for annuities, 0.8% for whole life based on 15 quarters' data, offsetting $40M crediting cap hikes amid 4.35% 10-year yields, mainly in $120B FIA.

Discount/longevity offset $15M unfavorable: +25 bps to 4.75% for PRT/group annuities, but LTC reserves up $25M for 3% higher incidence and Scale BB longevity (net tail margin at CTE95).

By segment: $215M life/annuity (FIA/IUL sales +22% to $8.5B), $55M health/LTC, $10M group/P&C. U.S. 85% dominant under PBR; Europe Solvency II longevity +0.5 years; Asia Japan mortality gains $15M.

AI platform with ML/GANs cuts uncertainty 30%; industry post-COVID trends suggest more unlocks.

This supports "Assumption Alpha" for 200 bps ROE lift: hedging $60B derivatives at 4.2% OAS via Apex Re; FIA 2.0 launches; $500M buybacks; climate/cyber buffers.

Q4 neutral-to-$100M favorable expected.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. Instructions for queuing. Our first question comes from Mike Johnson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Johnson: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the combined ratio improvements by segment, particularly personal lines?

Mark Thompson: Good morning, Mike. Happy to. Tom, want to add thoughts?

Tom Ellis: Sure, Mark. Mike, personal lines at 90.2% was outstanding. Auto's telematics push to 35% penetration helped tame frequency and severity, paired with those 8% rates. Homeowners took some cat hits but rate discipline and non-renewals in risky areas like Florida coasts kept it tight. Overall, it's proof our pricing actions are landing.

Laura Bennett: To add, Mike, the ex-cat trends are even stronger, positioning us for continued gains.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sarah Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Sarah Lee: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of the current rate environment on your investment yields and portfolio strategy?

Laura Bennett: Good morning, Sarah. The higher-for-longer rates have been a boon, pushing our yield to 4.25% with fixed income leading. We've locked in durations and built ladders for cuts, while alternatives like private credit offer buffers. Our ALM keeps us agile, with hedges covering key risks.

Mark Thompson: Yes, and it amplifies our float growth nicely.

Operator: Our next question from David Kim with Morgan Stanley.

David Kim: Thanks. On customer acquisition costs, how sustainable are those partnership gains, and any regional risks?

Laura Bennett: David, partnerships like embedded with Uber and ADP are scaling fast with low CAC and high attachment. Sustainability comes from API integrations and data moats. Asia risks like currency are hedged; Europe's regs are a watch but pilots help. Overall, very durable.

Operator: Next from Lisa Chen with Barclays.

Lisa Chen: Good morning. Regarding actuarial changes, how do you view longevity trends and their reserve implications?

Laura Bennett: Morning, Lisa. Longevity updates were conservative, building tail margins for LTC amid delayed care. Mortality improvements dominate positively, and our AI tuning ensures credibility. Peers are seeing similar, pointing to ongoing favorability if rates hold.

Operator: One more from Tom Patel with Citigroup.

Tom Patel: Quick one on capital deployment post these strong results.

Mark Thompson: Tom, our 520% RBC gives flexibility. We're executing the $1.2B repurchase and eyeing bolt-on growth, all while maintaining dividend strength.

Laura Bennett: Precisely, with assumption unlocks freeing more for shareholders.

Operator: Seeing no further questions at this time.

Mark Thompson: Thank you for your questions and your interest in EverSecure Insurance Group. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
